meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сетитель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A visitor was sitting in the reception room.

examples.text: Это журнал посетителей мэрии из полицейских вещдоков.
examples.trans: This is the mayor's visitor log from police evidence.

examples.text: Зато в ресторане станет больше посетителей.
examples.trans: On the other hand, there will be more patrons in the restaurant.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: That's what you said.
I speak Russian.
Well, the thing you said.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some, some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What nonsense.
Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?
Where is your room?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('familiar, known').

examples.text: А знакомо ли тебе, Аркашка, слово педикюр?
examples.trans: And are you familiar, Arkashka, with the word pedicure?

examples.text: Я услышал в коридоре знакомый голос.
examples.trans: I heard a familiar voice in the corridor.
I will call acquaintances right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
See the markers? They're from Japan!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мереть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to die', paired with 'умирать'.

examples.trans: She died last year.
He died very old.
But she died anyway.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
But you've still got some.
I told you: no.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
Can you smoke here?
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.
I'm a bit tired.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from; of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A letter from Mum.
I'm tired of work.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hide; to conceal', paired with 'скрыть'.

examples.text: Зачем ты скрывал правду от своей жены?
examples.trans: Why did you hide the truth from your wife?

examples.text: Ты явно скрываешь от меня правду.
examples.trans: You are clearly concealing the truth from me.

examples.text: Я не могу больше скрывать правду.
examples.trans: I can no longer hide the truth.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's no problem.
This time there's no trick.
That's no problem at all.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'captain' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Captain Gnezdo.
This is our captain.
Captain Gnezdo, Investigative Committee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лгода'). Common masculine noun meaning 'half a year, six months' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: In six months.
I've been here for six months now.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'walks'.

examples.text: Мальчик ходит на костылях. А она ещё и активистка.
examples.trans: The boy walks on crutches. And she's an activist, too.

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Ходила вокруг меня, как акула.
examples.trans: She was the one who met me! She circled around me like a shark.
She circled around me like a shark.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'язанный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('obliged, indebted').

examples.trans: I don't owe you anything.
You are obliged to come on time.

examples.text: Ты выпустишь меня под подписку о невыезде. И ты мне больше ничем не обязан.
examples.trans: You'll release me on a travel ban. And you won't owe me anything anymore.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'явиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to appear, to show up', paired with 'появляться'.

examples.text: Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: Let him just show up here one more time!
We came up with a good idea.

examples.text: Я тебе серьёзно говорю. Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: I'm telling you seriously. Let him just show up here one more time!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.trans: A new house.
I need a new job.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'head chef, executive chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

examples.text: Шеф-повар решит, подходите ли вы ресторану.
examples.trans: The head chef will decide whether you suit the restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'этому').

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.
I'm tired, so I'm at home.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'зволить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to allow, to permit', paired with 'позволять'.

examples.trans: Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.
Allow me to help you.

examples.text: Прошу, присаживайтесь. Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Please, have a seat. Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

представить.gloss: to imagine, to picture; to introduce

meanings.en: to imagine, to picture; to introduce
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to imagine, to picture; to introduce', paired with 'представлять'.

examples.text: Представь: тебе сорок лет, жена красавица.
examples.trans: Imagine: you're forty, with a beautiful wife.

examples.text: Представь: тебе сорок лет, жена красавица, дети, бизнес. А тебя все зовут врунишкой!
examples.trans: Imagine: you're forty, with a beautiful wife, children, a business. And everyone still calls you a little liar!

examples.text: Представь: тебе сорок лет, жена красавица, дети, бизнес.
examples.trans: Imagine: you're forty, with a beautiful wife, children, a business.
